argument_a_active_suppresses_own_output.identity: docs/math-foundations.md §1.1: N(T) = ⌊AS · u · T⌋ with swing timestamps t_i = i·Δ; ability recasts share ONE timeline and 'a cast counts when it *starts* within the window'.
argument_a_active_suppresses_own_output.computation: Syndra L18 (data/champions.json): base AS 0.658, AS ratio 0.625, AS growth 2%/lvl. Bonus AS% = 2 × 17 × (0.7025 + 0.0175 × 17) = 34 × 1.0 = 34%. AS = 0.658 + 0.625 × 0.34 = 0.8705. Over the scenario's 60 s window, u = 1: N(60) = ⌊0.8705 × 60⌋ = ⌊52.23⌋ = 52 autos. Two-and-a-half seconds of stasis remove 2.5/60 = 4.167% of the action window: N(57.5) = ⌊0.8705 × 57.5⌋ = ⌊50.05⌋ = 50 autos, i.e. −2 autos, plus every ability cast whose start epoch falls inside the frozen 2.5 s is pushed out of (or off the end of) the shared timeline.
argument_a_active_suppresses_own_output.conclusion: Time Stop *does* change outgoing TDD — it strictly reduces it. So the new reason's premise is false in the direction that matters: assuming the mechanic is 'durability only' would let a stasis be assumed for free, silently deleting ~4% of the action window from TDD (or, symmetrically, crediting durability without charging its damage cost).

argument_b_stat_block_is_offensive.computation: Zhonya's grants 105 AP (data/items.json stats.abilityPower.flat = 105.0). Syndra AP ratios from data/champions.json: Q Dark Sphere 70% AP, W Force of Will 65% AP, E Scatter the Weak 60% AP, R Unleashed Power minimum 60% AP. Σ ratios = 0.70 + 0.65 + 0.60 + 0.60 = 2.55. Raw magic damage added per full rotation by this item's stats = 105 × 2.55 = 267.75 (pre-mitigation).
argument_b_stat_block_is_offensive.conclusion: The item is not a pure defence on the stat side either.

reasoning_summary: The new value asserts two things that the cached data contradicts. (1) 'Every declared family on this item is a defence' — the stasis item declares control, damage, economy and stat families, including 105 flat AP, which for Syndra is worth 105 × 2.55 = 267.75 raw magic damage per rotation; and no item in the 324-object corpus has an all-defensive family set (every one declares economy). (2) 'the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD' — the cached wiki text says the holder is, for the 2.5 s duration, 'unable to move, declare basic attacks, cast abilities, use summoner spells, or activate items', so under the engine's own N(T) = ⌊AS·u·T⌋ / shared-cast-timeline identity a 2.5 s stasis inside the 60 s scenario window removes 4.167% of action time (Syndra L18: 52 → 50 autos, plus displaced casts). Time Stop therefore has a first-order, negative effect on outgoing TDD. That is precisely why the old reason is the correct one: the duration is bounded and the cached active carries no cooldown, so stasis seconds cannot be inferred from item presence and must come from an explicit bounded active-seconds scenario input.
verdict_detail: old_value_correct — the pre-change reason is supported by the cached wiki text, the atom provenance and the §1.1 scheduling identity; the post-change reason is factually false on both of its clauses for the only items in the corpus that carry the represented mechanic.
